heard: One bizarre nebula is colder than the Big Bang itself. Located 5,000 light years away in Centaurus, this object reaches a bone-chilling 1 Kelvin. While the afterglow of the Big Bang warms space to 2.7 Kelvin, the nebula plunges to minus 272 degrees Celsius. Astronomers Keith Taylor and Mike Scarot named it around 1980 after telescopes revealed a curved, asymmetrical shape. Later Hubble images exposed its true bow-tie form as a young planetary nebula. A dying central star is shedding mass up to 100 times faster than similar stars. Blasting gas outward at hundreds of thousands of kilometers per hour causes extreme adiabatic cooling. That rapid expansion drops temperatures below cosmic microwave radiation, explaining why.
